A global consumer-electronics giant's startup accelerator brought me in
mid-project as CTO, with $3M+ of investment already committed and the project in
motion before its real risks had been named. The vision was to record the audio
of a meeting from across the room, turn it into a clean transcript, summarize it,
and pull out the action items and assign them to the people who were there. In
2013, that was science fiction. Surfacing that honestly meant arguing against the
project's continuation, and against my own role in it. I made the call: a
non-starter with anything that existed then, which saved the $3M+ that would
otherwise have followed it in. I then took over as the team's CEO for the pivot
and delivered a working alpha ahead of schedule. The project was later defunded
and the team laid off. The value here was the honest call, not the outcome.
